turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Mr Byrne, come on through, yourself and your wife. I'll take your observations before Dr Kelly sees you. It has cleared up lovely after that rain.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Good morning. Thank you, nurse. Yes, it is pleasant to have the sun back.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Arm out straight for me, please. There we are. Blood pressure is 138 over 86, pulse 76, and the temperature is 36.6. All grand.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): That is reassuring. Thank you.
[SEG0005] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We are a little early, nurse. I hope that does not put anyone out.
[SEG0006] person_1 (NURSE): Not a bother. The doctor will be in in a tick. Sit yourselves down.
[SEG0007] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hello, come in. I am Dr Kelly. You are Declan, and this is?
[SEG0008] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Maureen, his wife. Thank you for fitting us in, doctor.
[SEG0009] person_4 (DOCTOR): You are very welcome. Declan, what can I do for you today?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Good morning, doctor. I am grateful you could see me. It is my lower back. It has become quite a bother.
[SEG0011] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He has been very quiet with it at home, doctor, but it is wearing on him.
[SEG0012] person_4 (DOCTOR): I am sorry. Tell me, in your own time, how it actually feels.

[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): It is a deep ache across the lower back, there most days, worse towards evening after the lifting, and it reaches the left buttock. It catches when I bend, though a hot water bottle or lying flat will ease it for a while. A bad day I would score as a six, or a seven if the pallets were heavy. It has been a few weeks, to my mind.
[SEG0014] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): A few weeks? Sure it began with the house move, Declan, you know—
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): If I might just finish, please. Yes, around that time, but I would not pin it to one morning. A few weeks is the figure I will stand over.
[SEG0016] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We moved six weeks ago on the Saturday. He carried the washing machine with his brother, and he has been crooked ever since, the pain going into the left buttock.
[SEG0017] person_4 (DOCTOR): So a few weeks by your account, and about six if we count from the move, with that heavy lifting in there. Does it travel any further than the buttock?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): It does reach the left buttock, as Maureen says, but no further. It does not run down the leg, not below the knee.
[SEG0019] person_4 (DOCTOR): Tell me about the work, if you would. What are the days like?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): I am a warehouse operative, doctor. The lifting is most shifts, and the low shelves mean a good deal of bending. I would not call it light work.
[SEG0021] person_4 (DOCTOR): How have the nights been, with this?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): It wakes me once or twice if I turn over. The nights are broken, though I would not say I am exhausted.
[SEG0023] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I hear him, and then I am awake myself, but that is hardly his fault.
[SEG0024] person_4 (DOCTOR): What have you been using for the pain?

[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): The orange capsules, doctor, the Nurofen. I take two of the two-hundred milligram ones at a time. There are plain white tablets as well, though I cannot tell you the proper name, and a white gel from the chemist for the back. I cannot mind the name of that gel, and the box is at home.

[SEG0026] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The white tablets are paracetamol from the chemist, five hundred milligrams. He takes two when the pain is bad, not every day. I do not know the gel either. It might be a heat rub, or it might be something else entirely.
[SEG0027] person_4 (DOCTOR): How often would the Nurofen be?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): It is not regular, I must admit. Twice on a quiet day, three times if it is fierce. I forget doses. I would not claim I take it as one ought to.
[SEG0029] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): There was the Difene as well. A lad at work gave him a strip.

[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. I believe they were the fifty milligram ones, though I am not certain of that. I took them for three or four days and then I stopped, because they gave me heartburn.
[SEG0031] person_4 (DOCTOR): We will leave the Difene aside. Any numbness, or pins and needles, in the legs or around the back passage?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): No, doctor. No numbness, and no pins and needles. The feeling in the skin is quite as usual.
[SEG0033] person_4 (DOCTOR): And passing water — any difficulty getting it started, or any leaking?
[SEG0034] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He is up in the night, doctor. I hear him on the landing.

[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): That is the tea in the evening, Maureen, and it has been so for years, long before this back. For your question, doctor, there is no difficulty passing water, and there have been no accidents.
[SEG0036] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any fever, or sweats, or feeling generally unwell?
[SEG0037] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Oh, before it goes out of my head, the car is on the yellow lines, and I meant to mention it to the—
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): No, doctor. No fever and no sweats. I feel well in myself, apart from the back.
[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): Have you lost weight without meaning to?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): I would not have thought so. My appetite is unchanged. The trousers sit a little easier, but our meals have been at all hours since the move.
[SEG0041] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His belt is on a new hole. I would say half a stone since Christmas, doctor, not only these last weeks.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): I do not accept half a stone, Maureen. We have not been on a scales. I feel the same weight, truly.
[SEG0043] person_4 (DOCTOR): Then we will not call the weight settled, and nobody weighed you this morning. I will examine you in a moment.
[SEG0044] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): While you are at the couch, doctor, did you see the hurling at the weekend? Our grandson was on the sideline with the little ones.
[SEG0045] person_4 (DOCTOR): I caught the second half on the wireless. That wind nearly took the posts.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): It turned into a fine afternoon once the shower passed. He is only six, and the jersey was far too big, but he was very proud.
[SEG0047] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His mother has him certain he will play in Croke Park. He told the whole table about a point, whether it was counted or not.
[SEG0048] person_4 (DOCTOR): Fair play to him. Six is a grand age for that sort of belief.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): The drive home was the slow part. Traffic from the grounds was very heavy, and we were late for the dinner my sister had on.
[SEG0050] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Desperate, the whole road. He fell asleep in the back with the boots still on, which was a picture.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): My sister was good about the dinner being late. She had made an apple tart, and he had two slices before anyone else sat down.
[SEG0052] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sunday roads, and a tart at the end of it. A good day, by the sound of things. Declan, would you stand just there, with your back to me?
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): Of course, doctor.
[SEG0054] person_4 (DOCTOR): There is tenderness in the muscles either side of the lower spine, a little more on the left. I do not see any redness, and there is no swelling.
[SEG0055] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. That is the spot.
[SEG0056] person_4 (DOCTOR): Bend forward, only as far as is comfortable. That will do. Flexion is limited by the pain. Up on the couch when you are ready.
[SEG0057] person_2 (PATIENT): Certainly. One moment while I get these shoes off.
[SEG0058] person_4 (DOCTOR): Straight leg raise is easy on both sides, with no pain shooting down. Power at the hips and feet is normal, sensation is intact, and the pulses in both feet are present.
[SEG0059] person_2 (PATIENT): I am relieved to hear that.

[SEG0060] person_4 (DOCTOR): I think this is a mechanical low back pain, the muscular kind that follows lifting, and not a nerve being pressed. I cannot fully set aside a little disc irritation, because the pain reaches the buttock, but there is no sign of a trapped nerve today.
[SEG0061] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you, doctor. That is clearer. What would you have me do?

[SEG0062] person_4 (DOCTOR): Keep moving, short walks, and do not take to the bed. The hot water bottle is fine. Ease off the heavy pallets for a week or two if the job allows, and bend at the knees rather than the back.
[SEG0063] person_2 (PATIENT): I will speak with the supervisor. He is reasonable, though if the orders are behind he does tend to—

[SEG0064] person_4 (DOCTOR): Do what you reasonably can. I would not have you laid up over it. For the tablets, stay with the paracetamol, two of the five-hundreds up to four times a day if you need them, and you may continue the Nurofen at four hundred milligrams up to three times a day, with food.
[SEG0065] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And if he forgets the middle one, as he does?
[SEG0066] person_4 (DOCTOR): Then he takes the next when it is due, and he does not double up. Leave the Difene out entirely.
[SEG0067] person_2 (PATIENT): Should there be an x-ray, doctor?

[SEG0068] person_4 (DOCTOR): Not for today. If it has not eased in two weeks, or sooner if you get numbness, trouble passing water, or weakness in a leg, we would arrange imaging and you would come straight in. If the pain is not settling in two weeks, come back and see me, and we might arrange physiotherapy then if it is still limiting you.
